newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa says no strings to support for Kabila.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa says no strings to support for Kabila.

text.p: South Africa has recognised Laurent Kabila as new president of Zaire without strings, but plans to offer him advice on ensuring democracy and stability, officials said on Monday.

"There are no 'buts' attached to our recognition of Kabila as the new president. There are no strings attached. The Deputy President is quite confident that this process will unfold as promised," Ricky Naidoo, spokesman for South African Deputy President Thabio Mbeki, told Reuters by telephone.
After two hours of talks with Kabila on Sunday, Mbeki said South Africa would immediately recognise Kabila as head of state following the departure of former president Mobutu Sese Seko.
Other governments recognised Kabila, too, but many added an exhortation to institute democratic structures as soon as possible and to demonstrate a commitment to human rights.

Naidoo said Mbeki would brief diplomats in Pretoria at midday on Monday about his meeting with Kabila and about the sort of technical assistance the new government might need to rebuild infrastructure destroyed under 32 years of Mobutu's rule.
Joel Netshitenzhe, senior spokesman for President Nelson Mandela, said South Africa had no doubts about Kabila's commitment to democracy and human rights.
"The fact of the matter is that a new government has taken over. The practicality of diplomacy and inter-state relations is that you have to deal with that new government.
"In support of our recognition, however, we will offer Mr Kabila advice on how to ensure a democratic and stable future for the entire nation.
"He should ensure, as soon as humanly possible, that structures are put in place to underpin democracy and legitimacy in the country," Netshitenzhe said.
Naidoo said Mbeki had briefed Mandela early on Monday about his meeting with Kabela before the president left on a state visit to neighbouring Zimbabwe.

He said Mandela and Mbeki would immediately begin a series of consultations with the United Nations, the Organisation of African Unity and regional leaders on how to help Zaire achieve long-term stability.
